newsitem.title: UK: Licht sees lower East European 96/97 sugar output.
newsitem.headline: Licht sees lower East European 96/97 sugar output.

text.p: East European sugar production should fall to 9.29 million tonnes in 1996/97 after the 9.71 million notched up a year previously, German statistician F.O. Licht said on Monday.
Output was expected to fall sharply in both Ukraine and Russia, the region's two largest producers, Licht said.
Ukrainian production was pegged at 3.15 million tonnes, compared with 3.78 million in 1995/96, and Russian production at 1.82 million after 2.24 million.
"Many things are still going wrong in Russia," Licht said in its first estimate of world sugar production for 1996/97.
It noted a smaller area sown to beet, adverse weather and lack of necessary inputs.
"The Ukraine has suffered from similar difficulties, consequently its crop will also be down."

But some east European nations were optimistic, Licht said, adding that the Czech Republic was hoping for a 17 percent increase in output and Poland was expecting to produce about two million tonnes after 1.7 million tonnes last season.
